title: flexible-commitment-window-and-soft-flood-control
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: some tenants have predictable burst patterns on weekly windows; others benefit from shorter commit cycles. This change introduces a per-tenant flexible commitment window to let Dedicated customers choose commit granularity (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d) and a 'soft flood control' mechanism that dampens microburst allocation to warm pools without hard rejecting requests. The PR includes config schema, autoscaler controller logic, admission gating, telemetry changes, and tests. Checklist: - [x] API/config schema + validation - [x] Autoscaler algorithm changes and unit tests - [x] Admission gate + best-effort fallback path - [x] Telemetry: percentile histograms + new warmpool_flood_metric - [x] Docs draft for admins and ops - [x] Backwards compatibility e2e scenarios

What changed (summary): expanded CommitmentPolicy to accept a window enum and a dynamic weight schedule; autoscaler computes provisional reservations at shorter windows and aggregates them for longer commitments; soft flood control applies a decaying credit multiplier when sequential short-window spikes exceed adaptive burst_thresholds; admission controller now emits hint headers (X-Redwood-Warmpool-Hint) for downstream warmpool agents to prefer soft-evict vs hard-reject; telemetry adds p95/p99 token_utilization histograms and a flood_score gauge per-tenant. Safety: default tenant config preserves existing 24h semantics unless overridden. Rollout plan: feature-flagged for internal Dedicated clusters, enable for 10% of tenants in canary, monitor warmpool drop and tail latency for three business days, then increase to 50%.
commits: feat(commits): add CommitmentWindow enum and per-tenant policy parsing
refactor(autoscaler): compute provisional reservations for sliding windows
feat(admission): implement soft flood control credit multiplier and hint headers
telemetry: expose warmpool_flood_score and token_utilization histograms
test: unit/e2e for flexible windows and soft flood scenarios
docs: admin guide draft and config examples
ci_checks: benchmarks: warn (hotpath allocations increased slightly on microbench; improved in follow-up)
release_notes: Introduce per-tenant flexible commitment windows and a soft flood control mechanism to smooth microbursts; adds telemetry for flood_score and utilization percentiles.
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Can we prove that shorter windows won't cause oscillations when combined with autoscaler backoff? Please add a stability test simulating 30s spikes and verify no churning.
Maya Chen: Added stability test simulating 30s microbursts in test/e2e/flexible_commit_window_test.go and tuned the provisional reservation dampener (see commit 4). Results attached to CI artifacts.
Elena Morales: Telemetry looks good; suggest adding a warmpool_flood_score tag for tier (standard/premium) to help downstream dashboards.
Maya Chen: Added tier label to flood_score and updated histograms.yaml.
Samir Gupta: Small nit: prefer name soft_flood_multiplier -> flood_decay_multiplier for clarity. Also update adm doc snippet to show header usage in curl examples.
Maya Chen: Renamed symbol and updated docs. Addressed all nits.
notes: Initial CI run failed on benchmarks; root cause was an allocator regression introduced by provisional reservation rounding. Fixed in second commit by switching to fixed-point arithmetic for small reservations.
Feature behind dedicated.feature_flags.flex_commit_window; safe to enable incrementally.
Observed: 12% reduction in warmpool evictions during 30s burst simulations in canary compared to baseline. Tail latency p99 improved by ~6ms for most tenants in canary group.
changelog_entry: Add per-tenant flexible commitment windows and soft flood control to reduce warmpool churn and offer shorter commit granularity for Dedicated tenants. Telemetry: warmpool_flood_score, token_utilization p95/p99 histograms.
